attempts.raw_response: The festival will also showcase the Coen Brothers' latest comedy, Inside Llewyn Davis, featuring Oscar Isaac as a struggling folk musician in 1960s New York. Horror fans can look forward to the Jim Jarmusch-directed Only Lovers Left Alive, starring Tilda Swinton and Tom Hiddleston as ancient vampires. The program includes the French film Blue Is the Warmest Colour, winner of the Palme d'Or, and the British historical drama The Invisible Woman, starring Ralph Fiennes as Charles Dickens. Documentary enthusiasts will appreciate The Act of Killing, an Indonesian film exploring the 1965 genocide through surreal reenactments. The festival closes with the premiere of The Wolf of Wall Street, Martin Scorsese's latest starring Leonardo DiCaprio.

pair.human_continuation: Toronto is now the leading film festival in North America and often serves as a launch pad for high-profile awards contenders. The event runs concurrently with the Venice Film Festival in Italy, which opens on 29 August with Mira Nair's film of 2007 novel The Reluctant Fundamentalist. That film will also screen at Toronto, as will Jayne Mansfield's Car - a family drama from the actor and film-maker Billy Bob Thornton that was seen earlier this year at Berlin. Another actor turned film-maker - one Dustin Hoffman - will unveil his directorial debut Quartet during the busy Toronto showcase. Costa-Gavras, Neil Jordan, Robert Redford and David O Russell are among the other notable directors to have films in the programme.
pair.prefix: Others include Cloud Atlas, an adaptation of the David Mitchell novel starring Hugh Grant and Halle Berry that was partly shot in Scotland. Ben Affleck drama Argo, about the rescue of US diplomats from Iran in 1979, will also make its debut. So will an adaptation of Salman Rushdie's 1980 Booker winner Midnight's Children, directed by India's Deepa Mehta. New versions of Dickens's Great Expectations, Tolstoy's Anna Karenina and Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing are also in the line-up.

source_document.title: Looper to launch Toronto film festival
